text:
Liam (sales): Quick help — Nexa Financial wants a POC perf run tomorrow. Target: p95 < 250ms for chat workloads with ~2k concurrent active users (avg 1 req/sec per user during peak), avg response ~350 tokens. Need an actionable load plan and a short writeup we can share with their infra/security team. Who can lead?

Alex K: I can take lead on the load plan. Quick clarifying q: are they using streaming completions or full-response? Streaming changes latencies and connection counts.

Liam (sales): Full-response for now (no SSE). They may test streaming later.

Alex K: Ok. Plan outline: 1) warm-up to populate prefix/KV cache, 2) ramp to 2k concurrent over 5m, 3) sustain 30m, 4) burst tests (4k for 2m), 5) graceful cooldown. Measure p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and connection failures. Use our Dedicated canary endpoint.

Alex K: Suggested load tool + example (vegeta):
```
echo "POST https://canary.api.redwood-inference/v1/chat/completions" | vegeta attack -rate=2000 -duration=30m -connections=6000 | vegeta report -type=json
```
Notes: adjust -connections to simulate simultaneous clients; set request body with typical prompt sizes (avg 350 tokens).

Jess S: Infra notes — run from two regions to catch cross-AZ variability. Monitor GPU util, queue depth, and per-node token/sec. If p99 > 1s, enable batching or scale out one more node. Also watch ephemeral connection limits on the client side.

Maya R: Buyer question on pricing: if they need burst capacity (2h/day) what’s delta vs committed dedicated? Need a short answer to include in the one-pager.

Samir P: Shortball: burst add-on ~35–50% over base hourly for that incremental capacity depending on model and quantization. I'll run a 2-hour sim for exact numbers and post a small table.

Alex K: Quick perf snapshot from my lab sim (matches our canary config): at 2k concurrent, avg resp ~350 tokens — p50=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=470ms, errors ~0.2%. If their requirement is p99 < 300ms we need either lower model latency (smaller/quantized model), stronger caching, or an extra spare node for headroom.

Liam (sales): Can someone convert Alex's sim into a 1-page results writeup we can send tomorrow? Include commands, config, and a cost delta for burst vs sustained.

Jess S: I'll draft the runbook + results graphs. Samir, please drop the cost table. Alex, attach the raw vegeta JSON. I'll assemble into a PDF and add our ops notes for their infra team.

Samir P: On it. Also flagging security asks: they want IP allowlist + short SOC2/SSO checklist. Maya, can you attach our security brief?

Maya R: Yep — I'll attach the security brief and a one-paragraph note about VPC peering and certs. Targeting EOD tomorrow for delivery.

Alex K: EOD works. Recommendation in the writeup: 2 Dedicated nodes for steady state + 1 burst node to absorb the 4k short bursts. Also include tuning: enable KV prefix cache, lower decoding max tokens where acceptable, and consider int8 quant for tail reduction.

perf-bot: load-test-complete: summary attached (p50:72ms, p95:210ms, p99:470ms, errors:0.2%) :bar_chart:

Liam (sales): Awesome — thanks team. I'll update Nexa and schedule a follow-up demo.

Jess S: Action items recap: Alex — write the raw run outputs and commands; Samir — cost scenarios (sustained vs burst); Maya — security brief & checklist; Jess — assemble final one-pager and send. I'll own delivery to the prospect.

Liam (sales): Perfect. :thumbsup:
